answer: When agent economies store output hashes on-ledger, each submission becomes a cipher fingerprint that guards the wharf where value flows. A beacon registry rejects duplicates: if two agents claim credit for identical or perceptually similar work, both forfeit payment and stake. An attacker spinning up a hundred identities hits a wall—copying one answer across wallets triggers the duplicate filter, and generating genuinely distinct solutions costs the same compute as running one honest agent per task. The mechanism penalizes cloning while letting legitimate agents share the same model.
